options.title: Why Did the Tacoma Narrows Bridge Twist Itself Apart?
options.first_line: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge tore itself apart in a {fact2} mile-an-hour wind. How does wind do that?
options.first_frame: In 3D over grey water, the green suspension bridge's deck is twisting, one edge up and one down, the mid-span already amber, with the caption NOV 1940 · TACOMA NARROWS and a wind readout on a gauge by the tower.

options.title: Galloping Gertie: The Bridge the Wind Tore Apart
options.first_line: Drivers called the Tacoma Narrows Bridge Galloping Gertie. Then one morning, the wind tore it apart. How?
options.first_frame: A lone car on the rolling deck of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge, the road ahead rising like a wave, the caption NOV 1940 · TACOMA NARROWS on top.

options.title: A Steel Bridge vs a Steady Wind: Why Did Tacoma Lose?
options.first_line: A steady wind beat a brand-new steel bridge at Tacoma Narrows. How does wind win against steel?
options.first_frame: Side by side: a wind arrow streaming across the water and the bridge's solid steel side, the deck starting to tilt, the caption NOV 1940 · TACOMA NARROWS.

why: A famous bridge visibly twisting in the first frame, plus a modest wind figure, makes a stranger ask how ordinary wind could do that, and neither the title nor the first line gives the answer.
